neighbours.label: a pushed or pulled wheeled conveyance without its own engine (cart, trolley, wagon, chariot, carriage, stroller), as against self-propelled vehicles (car, bus, bicycle)
fire: At the airport he piled our suitcases onto a luggage trolley and hurried inside.
Two donkeys pulled the heavy cart up the muddy track to the village.
In the museum we saw a gilded Roman chariot with spoked wheels.
The pioneers repaired a broken wheel on their wagon before crossing the river.
Every morning the old man pushed his fruit cart through the narrow streets.
The cleaner wheeled her trolley of towels down the hotel corridor.
Visitors can ride around the estate in a carriage drawn by two grey ponies.
On the farm the children loved riding in the hay wagon behind the tractor.
quiet: At the airport he loaded our suitcases into a taxi and hurried inside.
Two tourists drove the heavy jeep up the muddy track to the village.
In the museum we saw a vintage Roman coin with a stamped emperor.
The pioneers repaired a broken fence on their land before crossing the river.
Every morning the old man rode his motorbike through the narrow streets.
The cleaner carried her pile of towels down the hotel corridor.
Visitors can ride around the estate in a minibus driven by a guide.
On the farm the children loved riding on the tractor with their uncle.
